verdict: Good app, but not top-tier yet
verdict_explanation: For a static marketing site, the architecture is commendably flat: a single site.ts content module feeding all components, no costume layers, no redundant seams. The structural findings are real but local — a Schema.org honesty leak, a parallel icons array that silently mismaps on content growth, and BASE_URL construction scattered across 9 call sites in 7 files. None is catastrophic; all are fixable in targeted loops.

architecture_quality.proof: src/content/site.ts flat DAG with `as const`; components as pure template leaves. Residual: parallel icons array at BenefitGrid.astro:4-8; BASE_URL pattern repeated across 7 files.

state_management.proof: src/content/site.ts:206 — `as const` literal; zero mutable runtime state; static site generator pipeline; no writers, no readers, no persistence seam.

domain_modeling.proof: site.ts as const centralizes all content. Residual: icons (visual concern) co-located in BenefitGrid.astro as parallel array rather than in site.ts alongside the benefit data they annotate.

data_flow.proof: import { site } from '../content/site' is the single data source; all 8 components and 3 pages import from it. DAG is clean — no back-channels. Residual: BASE_URL transformation repeated at 9 call sites across 7 files with two inconsistent patterns.

framework_idioms.proof: Astro idioms used correctly — slot layout composition, Astro.props interface typing, loading=lazy/decoding=async on images. Residual: BaseLayout.astro:53 generates astro(4000) hint; Schema.org offers block references no Astro site data.

concurrency.proof: No async/await, no Promise, no event handlers, no Task constructs in any source file. Astro SSG builds synchronous template trees at build time. Concurrency is genuinely N/A for a static site generator.

simplicity.proof: Hero.astro:22-77 contains 55-line hardcoded HTML device mockup with 12 fixed tile labels disconnected from site.ts, plus ~165 CSS lines. BenefitGrid.astro:4-8 parallel icons array adds implicit invariant.

test_strategy.proof: Zero test files in repo. astro check provides type correctness only. No behavioral, semantic, or integration tests. 9-anchor (tests targeting real Interfaces) is not met.

credibility.proof: Schema.org structured data at src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro:60-63 claims price: '0' for a paid one-time-purchase app (site.pricing.pro.price = 'One-time purchase' at site.ts:167). Visible honesty leak.

strengths: site.ts as const centralizes all domain copy with zero framework imports — genuine content centralization, not fake-clean reward
FAQList.astro typed interface Props with limit/showCta parameters — callers in control, no ambient state
BaseLayout.astro Astro slot composition — header/footer composed without duplication; deletion test passes

findings.title: Schema.org structured data claims free pricing for a paid app
findings.why_it_matters: Search crawlers ingest JSON-LD and may surface misleading rich results showing price: $0 for a paid one-time-purchase app.
findings.what_is_wrong: BaseLayout.astro:60-63 hardcodes 'price': '0', 'priceCurrency': 'USD' in the Schema.org SoftwareApplication offer. site.pricing.pro.price = 'One-time purchase' (site.ts:167) and the free tier has no numeric price field. The schema falsely claims all versions are free.
findings.leverage_impact: None: the offer object is a 3-line inline literal; no leverage gained or lost.
findings.locality_impact: Low: offer defined in one place (BaseLayout.astro:60-63) but doesn't reference site.pricing — the honest source of truth is two files away.
findings.metric_signal: Astro build hint astro(4000) on BaseLayout.astro:53 — the same script tag containing the bad data.
findings.why_weakens_submission: A judge reading source sees PricingCard.astro correctly renders 'One-time purchase' while JSON-LD in the layout claims price: 0. The discrepancy is a honesty leak a production code reviewer would flag immediately.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Remove the offers block entirely from the Schema.org JSON-LD (Schema.org does not require it for SoftwareApplication), or emit a factually correct entry only for the free tier (price: '0' is truthful for the free plan). Also add is:inline directive to the script tag to silence the astro(4000) hint.

findings.title: BenefitGrid parallel icons array silently mismatches on content growth
findings.why_it_matters: Adding a fourth benefit to site.ts produces a silently-broken card with no icon, undetectable until visual QA.
findings.what_is_wrong: BenefitGrid.astro:4-8 defines const icons = [svg1, svg2, svg3] (3 entries). At line 15, site.benefits.map((benefit, i) => ... icons[i]) indexes into this array. site.benefits has 3 entries (site.ts:26-39). If a fourth benefit is added, icons[3] is undefined and Fragment set:html renders empty — no TypeScript error, no build warning.
findings.leverage_impact: Callers (editors of site.ts) cannot know that adding a benefit without also updating BenefitGrid.astro breaks the UI.
findings.locality_impact: Change spreads: a domain content change (site.ts) requires a parallel implementation change (BenefitGrid.astro) with no mechanical enforcement.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Silently broken UI on any content growth. The parallel array is a maintenance hazard that a code reviewer would flag as an invariant violation.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Move SVG icon strings into each benefit entry in site.ts as an `icon` field. Template reads benefit.icon directly. TypeScript enforces field presence — missing icon = type error at build time.

findings.title: BASE_URL construction repeated at 9 call sites across 7 files with inconsistent patterns
findings.why_it_matters: Any URL convention change requires touching 7 files with two inconsistent patterns that can produce broken links on GitHub Pages.
findings.what_is_wrong: Two construction patterns: (1) ${BASE_URL}${link.href.replace(/^\//, '')} in SiteHeader.astro:19,33; (2) bare ${BASE_URL}support concatenation in SiteFooter.astro:10-12, FAQList.astro:33, support.astro:71-73. Pattern 2 works only because literals happen not to have leading slashes. Changing SiteFooter's href to '/support' would produce double-slash on GitHub Pages.
findings.leverage_impact: Each call site must independently know the BASE_URL transformation rule including the slash-stripping quirk.
findings.locality_impact: URL convention change requires touching 7 files; inconsistency means some sites are more fragile than others.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Inconsistent URL construction is the kind of thing that ships a broken link to production. On GitHub Pages, BASE_URL is /benchhype-site/ so BASE_URL/support produces /benchhype-site//support.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extract a url(path: string): string helper in src/utils/url.ts: export const url = (path: string) => `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}${path.replace(/^\//, '')}`. All 9 call sites become url('support'), url('/'), etc. Deletion test passes: removing helper forces complexity back to 9 callers.

findings.title: Hero device mockup is 220 lines of hardcoded simulation disconnected from site.ts
findings.why_it_matters: Tile labels and player title in the hero visual will drift from the real app's content with zero build-time warning.
findings.what_is_wrong: Hero.astro:28-63 contains 12 hardcoded .sb-tile labels (Airhorn, Anthem, Crowd, Whistle, Buzzer, Organ, Defense, Strike, Charge, Timeout, Slap, Win) and player title 'Game Opener Mix' (Hero.astro:67), all disconnected from site.ts. ~165 lines CSS for the mockup.
findings.leverage_impact: None: the mockup is pure HTML/CSS with no reuse.
findings.locality_impact: Changes to app tile naming require manual hunting in Hero.astro, not site.ts.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Maintenance drift between hero visual and real app is invisible. Visitors read tile labels in the hero that may not match the actual app.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Replace the hardcoded device mockup with a real screenshot from site.screenshots[0] framed in the existing .device-frame CSS, or source tile labels from a site.ts heroTiles array. Option (a) is simpler — removes ~50 HTML lines and ~120 CSS lines.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: F1 fix removes a factual inaccuracy from Schema.org structured data — passes deletion test (offers block can be omitted without breaking anything).
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: Removing or correcting the offers block in BaseLayout is purely subtractive — fewer lines, more honest.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Adding a complex pricing-aware Schema.org renderer; introducing content module dependency on pricing just for JSON-LD.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: No tests exist; no test changes. astro check is the verification gate — it will still pass with 0 errors.

backlog.title: Correct Schema.org structured data — remove or fix the offers price block
backlog.why_it_matters: Honesty leak: search crawlers see free pricing for a paid one-time-purchase app. Also silences the astro(4000) hint by adding is:inline to the script tag.
backlog.score_impact: Overall implementation credibility +0.5, Framework/platform best practices +0.5

backlog.title: Inline icons into site.ts benefit entries, remove BenefitGrid parallel array
backlog.why_it_matters: Silent UI breakage on content growth; invariant not enforced by type system.

backlog.title: Extract url() helper to consolidate BASE_URL construction across 7 files
backlog.why_it_matters: 7-file touch radius for URL convention change; two inconsistent patterns that can produce broken links.

deepening_candidates.source_friction_proven: Finding F2 — icons array indexed against benefits with no enforcement
deepening_candidates.why_shallow_or_misplaced: Icon-to-benefit mapping is implicit runtime association; interface (edit site.ts) does not expose the constraint (also update BenefitGrid.astro).
deepening_candidates.behavior_to_move_behind_interface: Move icon SVGs into site.ts benefits[].icon field; template reads benefit.icon directly — no index.
deepening_candidates.test_surface_after_change: No tests. Build-time TypeScript enforces field presence.
deepening_candidates.smallest_first_step: Add icon: string field to each benefit in site.ts; update BenefitGrid.astro to use benefit.icon.
deepening_candidates.what_not_to_do: Do not extract an icon component or introduce a mapping object. Keep as string field in the data.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Any map(..., i) => sideArray[i] pattern where two arrays are maintained separately.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Co-locate associated data in the same object. If an icon belongs to a benefit, it is a property of the benefit, not an entry in a parallel array.
builder_notes.stack_example: In site.ts: benefits: [{ title: '...', body: '...', icon: '<svg>...</svg>' }] — icon travels with the benefit.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Same env var read + string transform repeated in 7+ files across the codebase.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: One function url(path) that owns the convention. All callers use it. Deletion test: if you delete the function, the problem comes back in all callers — it earns its keep.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: JSON-LD in a layout that contains prices, dates, or feature flags that also appear in a separate content module.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Either derive JSON-LD values from the content module (DRY), or omit claims the code cannot authoritatively make. Free tier can claim price=0 honestly; pro tier cannot claim a price until one is finalized.
builder_notes.stack_example: BaseLayout.astro: derive offer price from site.pricing.free (truthfully free) and omit the pro offer until a numeric price exists.

narrative: Place — good, not winning. The architecture is honestly flat: site.ts as the single content source feeding pure template leaves is the right pattern for a static site, and it's executed cleanly. The structural weaknesses are concentrated: a Schema.org honesty leak misrepresents pricing to search crawlers, a parallel icons array will silently break on content growth, and BASE_URL construction is scattered across 7 files with two inconsistent patterns. These are all fixable in 2-3 loops. Test strategy is effectively zero — for a pure static site this is less damning than for an app, but there are no behavioral checks of any kind. Concurrency and state management are genuinely N/A and scored 10 honestly. Future risk: the hero device mockup (220 hardcoded lines disconnected from site.ts) will drift from the real app's UI as the app ships.

loop_result.what_changed: Fixed src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro: added is:inline directive to JSON-LD script tag; restructured offers block to truthfully represent only the free tier (site.pricing.free.title, price: '0'); replaced hardcoded operatingSystem string with site.iosRequirement.
loop_result.evidence_change_is_honest: npm run build: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints (was 1 hint astro(4000) pre-fix). 5 pages built. astro check clean.

implementation_review.reason: All three checks passed; F1 (Schema.org free-price claim on all tiers) is no longer present in source; offers array correctly scoped to free tier only; astro(4000) hint eliminated; no regression introduced.
